title: Quantile-anchored multi-signal rollback controller for canaries and A/B cohorts
creator: Aisha Verma
description:
Problem: Canary and A/B rollouts occasionally trigger noisy or brittle rollbacks when using single-threshold checks (e.g., p95 latency > X). We want a controller that combines multiple SLO signals (latency quantiles, request error rate, token cost per request, throughput) into a stable, tunable rollback decision that adapts to cohort traffic patterns and reduces false positives while preserving fast remediation for real regressions.

Goal: Implement a quantile-anchored multi-signal rollback controller that: (1) computes cohort-aware baselines using historical quantiles, (2) applies asymmetric hysteresis per-signal, (3) aggregates signals with cost-weighted scoring, and (4) exposes tunable hyperparameters and autosuggested thresholds via the Console. The controller should be usable for canaries, A/B tests, and shadow traffic experiments.

Scope: Backend controller service + Console controls + monitoring dashboards + e2e test harness. Does NOT include new kernel/runtime changes; uses existing observability pipelines.

Success criteria: (a) Reduce rollback false-positive rate on historical canaries by >= 45% on our sampled dataset, (b) detect real regressions within 2 min for severity-high incidents, (c) Console shows recommended thresholds and simulated rollback score for an arbitrary model cohort.
acceptance_criteria: Controller implements per-cohort baseline computation using rolling quantiles (p50,p75,p90,p95,p99) over a configurable lookback window.
Supports inputs: latency distribution, request error rate (4xx/5xx), token cost per request, throughput (rps).
Aggregation model: cost-weighted score with configurable signal weights exposed in Console.
Hysteresis: per-signal asymmetric backoff/forgiveness to avoid flip-flopping; tunable via rollout policy.
Automated canary policy can be attached to a rollout to trigger: pause, partial rollback, or full rollback based on score thresholds.
Dashboard and PromQL/Tracing queries included for all signals; unit + integration tests for decision logic present.
Documentation and runbook for incident response and manual override are added to Confluence.
comments: 2026-02-21 — Aisha Verma: Kickoff meeting notes: scope agreed (controller + console + dashboards). Decided to reuse existing metrics pipeline and avoid adding new runtime hooks in initial iteration.
2026-02-27 — Mateo Chen: Early prototype implemented for quantile baselining; found p99 is extremely noisy for low-volume cohorts. Added cohort minimum traffic threshold to avoid spurious signals.
2026-03-03 — Priya Nair (SRE): Recommended adding a short sampling jitter window before evaluating canary score to avoid 1-minute scrape boundary artifacts.
2026-03-05 — Design review (Leah Park): Console UI mockups reviewed; requested an additional 'simulate rollout' mode that replays historical traffic against config to preview rollback probability.
2026-03-08 — Mateo Chen: Integration tests green for aggregation logic. Still failing flaky test with shadow traffic replay harness — investigating seeding and replay timings.
2026-03-10 — Product review (Daniel Kim): Approved prioritization; requested a default policy for P1 customers and a permissive starter template for self-serve users.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary-sim): implement core controller logic and a dry-run mode that emits rollback_score metrics but does not act.
Phase 2 (limited canary): wire controller to canary engine for small internal rollouts with manual approval gating.
Phase 3 (opt-in self-serve): Console exposes policy templates and simulation UI; enable for a subset of customers.
Phase 4 (default policies): ship sane defaults and on-call runbook; monitor and iterate after two weeks of production data.
tradeoffs: Complex aggregation reduces false positives but increases mental model complexity for operators — mitigated by simulation and recommended templates.
Using quantiles rather than mean improves robustness to long tails but needs careful volume thresholds for small cohorts.
Hard rollback thresholds are easy to reason about but brittle; score-based decisions require trust via observability and simulation.
